Tasks

Each task is a short request from a user. The model sees the request and a list of tools, decides whether and how to call them, gets the tool results back and answers. A task passes only when the calls, their arguments and order, and the resulting account state are right; on restraint tasks, only when no tool is called. 42 tasks per track, 7 of each type, 3 repetitions each.

The 8 finance tools

  • get_price: The current price of a stock or coin (AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, BTC, ETH) in a chosen currency.
  • get_ohlc: Daily open, high, low and close prices for a date range.
  • get_balance: How much cash the paper account holds, per currency.
  • get_positions: How much of each stock or coin the paper account holds.
  • convert: Converts an amount between USD, EUR, GBP and JPY at fixed rates.
  • place_order: Places a dry-run buy or sell order (market or limit) on the paper account; nothing is traded.
  • cancel_order: Cancels an open dry-run limit order and releases the money or coins it held back.
  • search_news: Searches a fixed set of made-up headlines by text and date.

Decoy tools

22 tools that have nothing to do with finance (get_weather, list_calendar, search_email, translate_text, set_alarm, find_recipe, …). Some selection and restraint tasks offer all 30 tools, the 8 finance tools and the decoys together. They test whether the model still picks the right tool from a long list, and leaves an unrelated tool alone just because it is there.

The six task types

  • Single call: One tool call with the right arguments, then the answer.
  • Tool selection: Pick the right tool from a long list that includes unrelated decoys.
  • Arguments: Exact argument values and formats: dates, tickers, currencies, empty or default fields.
  • Multi-step: Several calls in a row, where later calls use earlier results and the account state must end right.
  • Restraint: No tool fits, or the request asks for something the tools cannot do: the right answer calls nothing and invents nothing.
  • Recovery: A deliberate error (an unknown ticker, too little cash, a rate limit) that must be handled as instructed.

Renamed tools

Every task also exists in a renamed version: the same request and the same tools, but every tool and argument has a neutral name (get_price becomes fetch_quote, symbol becomes ticker). A model that only recognises familiar names fails there; a model that reads the tool descriptions does not. Both versions are scored, and the Renamed tools tab shows them side by side.

Synthetic only

All data are fixed synthetic fixtures (prices, balances, news), "today" is 2026-11-12, and orders are dry runs on a paper account. Nothing touches a market or a real account, and no real trade is ever made.

Not published

The tasks themselves, their expected answers and the models' replies are not published, so models cannot be trained on them. The tool definitions and each task's pass or fail (by task id) are. The "Public" and "Private" columns split the scores by an older public/private task split. Tool definitions · Tool definitions, renamed · Per-task results (pass/fail by task id)

Hard set

A second, harder set of 24 tasks per track (also in a renamed version) tests longer chains and stricter instruction following. A task that says "in this order" is graded in that order; an order call sent together with other calls in one message counts as a format failure, because the model must see each order result first. Same tools, fixtures and grading; 4 tasks of each type:

  • Long chain: 4 to 6 dependent calls; each argument comes from earlier results.
  • Computed arguments: Date arithmetic, currency conversion, rounding to whole units, totals across holdings.
  • Multi-constraint: Two or three rules at once: order, size cap, forbidden tool or currency, "only if".
  • Branching: The next step depends on fetched values, including cases where the right action is to do nothing.
  • Cascading recovery: Two different errors in one task (rate limit, then too little cash, ...), each handled as instructed.
  • Long output: Find the right value inside a long price history or a crowded account.

Blocked, incomplete, not ranked

These runs stopped because some requests ended without a complete reply (the client gave up at 600 s while the model was still generating). Those requests may have been answered later, so the missing results are not a random sample: no percentage, score, tier or rank is given. Counts only; the runs were not resumed or repeated.

Methodology

All tool observations use fixed synthetic finance fixtures, never real trades. Model answers are measured independently; tool-calling scores in model cards are maker-reported.

Original and renamed tracks are paired. Three repetitions per task; serving/configuration and verified template failures remain unscored. Public and private scores are separate; only public per-task details leave local storage.

Size class by total parameters, the same figures as the suite's other benches (from the maker's card, checked against the exact weights run): Tiny under 6B, Small 6B–15B, Medium over 15B up to 40B, Large over 40B.

No chance correction is applied. Tiers within each size class: for each pair of setups, every task (42 per track, public and private) is one paired item, won by the setup that passed more of its 3 repetitions; ties drop out. Exact two-sided sign test, Holm-corrected over all pairs of the class, p < 0.05. Rows in accuracy order: the top row starts Tier 1, and a row starts the next tier when the test separates it from its tier's top row. Accuracy: both tracks (84 tasks); Renamed tools: each track (42 tasks). – : not tiered (class not verified, incomplete or not qualified). Every pair's wins, losses, ties and p-values. Hard set: the same test over its 24 tasks per track; its pairs. Unknown cost and tokens stay unreported.

Decision models (Ümit #10795: the top 16 over 15B by Logic & Math score, and all 32 of 15B and under, open weights, our GPU only): each was served as a plain chat model, so these rows test its weights with a standard tool-calling interface, not its maker's decision engine. Scored: Elephant-1, KnowLine-9B-Gen2, Mammoth-1. Not qualified: GLiDE 0.8B and 2B (no tool call). Blocked, incomplete and not ranked: KnowLine-12B-Gen1 and KnowLine-31B-Gen2 (counts in the Blocked section; KnowLine-12B thinking on: its single qualification request was still generating at the 600 s client timeout). Not run, not servable as a chat model: GLiDE 9B, GLiDE 27B and GLiDE (no output layer in the weights), Karpo Decision 31B (vLLM cannot map its weight names), d3, d3-ultra and Drex Max (embedding-only), d1-2B (custom code, no output layer), GLiDE 0.4B (no chat template). Not run, other: REAX 1.3 and StartLux-Decision 9B and 4B (the local copy is an adapter or engine format, not full chat weights), and the remaining 29 of the 48 requested, whose weights are not on our server (incl. Logits Sigma-1 Duo, 57B). Paid API-only decision models were not run.
